market_name: Putin out as President of Russia by December 31, 2026?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether the Polymarket probability move is corroborated by any credible newswire (Reuters/Bloomberg) or is isolated market noise; note oil futures tick direction.
time_plan.1h: Compare Brent/WTI move vs baseline energy-sector moves to see if oil is actually reacting to the Russia signal or to broader macro.
time_plan.2h: Reassess whether implied vol in oil options has risen; a vol spike without clear direction supports 'unclear' classification.
time_plan.6h: Look for official Kremlin statements or denial; most such rumors reverse, so check if the prediction-market probability has decayed back.
time_plan.12h: Evaluate net oil move vs the 700bps tradable threshold; document whether the signal produced any durable directional edge or reverted to noise.

predictions.reasoning: Russia is one of the world's largest oil exporters, so any sharp repricing of 'Putin out' probability signals a regime-stability shock. The directional implication is genuinely ambiguous: a sudden removal/chaos scenario implies supply-disruption risk premium (oil up), while a scenario interpreted as a path to peace/sanctions relief implies more Russian barrels returning (oil down). Over a 12h window with only a probability shift (no confirmed event), the signal is weak and the proxy's response is dominated by other macro flows.

predictions.tradable_instrument_name: Select STOXX Europe Aerospace & Defense ETF

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Confirm whether the probability move reflects an actual news catalyst versus thin-market noise.
time_plan.1h: Check defense-sector price action vs broad European indices to isolate any conflict-driven repricing.
time_plan.2h: Monitor Ukrainian/Russian official commentary and any ceasefire-related headlines that would clarify direction.
time_plan.6h: Reassess whether the political-instability narrative is strengthening (escalation) or being framed as peace-path (de-escalation).
time_plan.12h: Document net move vs 700bps threshold; note that absence of a confirmed regime event most likely leaves this proxy range-bound.

predictions.reasoning: A shift in Putin's tenure probability alters the perceived trajectory of the Russia-Ukraine conflict. A succession/instability scenario could be read as either escalation risk (bullish defense) or a path toward de-escalation and lower long-run defense spending (bearish defense). Because both narratives are plausible and a probability shift is far from a confirmed event, the net effect on European defense names over 12h is highly uncertain and likely small.

evidence_used: Market question on Putin ceasing to be Russian President by end-2026
Resolution hinges on resignation, removal, detention, or incapacity
Russia's central role as a major oil/gas exporter and party to the Ukraine war
No liquid direct Russia equity proxies remain investable post-2022 sanctions
uncertainty_notes: Directional sign is fundamentally ambiguous: regime chaos (risk-premium up) vs peace path (supply relief, risk-off reversal)
A probability shift is a low-base-rate tail signal, not a confirmed event; most such rumors decay within hours
12h window is too short for a political-tenure thesis to resolve into clean asset moves
Proxies (oil, defense) respond to many unrelated macro drivers, diluting any Russia-specific signal

llm_justification.summary: A sharp repricing of 'Putin out by 2026' would flag Russian regime-stability risk, whose most liquid public-market expressions are crude oil and European defense equities. However, the directional implication is genuinely two-sided (instability/supply-disruption premium vs peace-path/sanctions-relief), and over a 12h window a mere probability shift without a confirmed event is a weak, noisy signal. Both mapped proxies are rated unclear/mixed with low confidence and expected moves below the 700bps tradable threshold.
key_assumptions: The prediction-market probability move is at least partially information-bearing rather than pure noise
No official confirmation of Putin's removal occurs within the window
Oil and defense ETFs remain the best available liquid proxies for Russia regime risk given delisted Russian equities
failure_modes: The move is isolated Polymarket noise with no real-world catalyst, so no asset reacts
The event is a false rumor that reverses within hours, reversing any initial asset move
Oil moves in the opposite direction expected because markets price peace/sanctions relief rather than supply disruption
Defense and oil proxies are swamped by unrelated macro flows, making the Russia signal undetectable
Information was already public/priced, so the prediction market lags rather than leads the asset move
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
